name: Darkmist Cavern
summary: Darkmist spiders swarm the old mine in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh. Ruined shacks stand by its entrance, and locals still dispute whether cave or brood bore the name first.

sections.title: The Brood in the Mine
sections.body:
Rotting shacks stand outside Darkmist Cavern in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh. Thick webs choke the tunnels. People once came here for the mine, but no human presence remains. Now Darkmist spiders fill its passages. Their size and venom make them deadly to unwary wanderers.

Marsh dwellers still dispute how the cavern got its name. Some say it was named for the brood nesting inside. Others say the spiders took their name from the misty cave.

sections.title: Hermit's Larder
sections.body: Even this web choked cavern draws scavengers. The hermit ‘Swamp Eye’ Jarl sends travelers deep into its webs to gather the eyes of monstrous spiders. He claims they make fine broth. Most sensible travelers keep clear of the web strewn entrance.

faq.answer: Darkmist Cavern is an abandoned mine in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh, now filled with giant, venomous Darkmist spiders.

faq.q: Who lived at the ruins outside the cave?
faq.answer: The ruins outside the cave suggest a settlement or mining camp once stood there, but no one knows who lived there.

faq.q: Why do locals venture into Darkmist Cavern?
faq.answer: Few willingly enter Darkmist Cavern. The hermit ‘Swamp Eye’ Jarl sends daring travelers into its tunnels to retrieve spider eyes for his strange marsh stew.

faq.q: Did the spiders or the cavern get the name first?
faq.answer: Dustwallow Marsh’s inhabitants disagree over whether the cavern was named for the spiders or the spiders for the cavern. No settled account says which name came first.

angles.text: The hermit ‘Swamp Eye’ Jarl calls Darkmist spider eyes the finest ingredient for marsh stew. Few beyond the swamp share his taste.
Miners once hollowed out the cavern. Anyone hoping to prospect its rocky depths must first face the nesting spiders.
